subject.title: /new and /reset should support @agent targeting in multi-agent channels

question: What should `/new` and `/reset` do in a multi-agent channel when no explicit agent target is supplied?
rationale: Current code can carry native command target sessions, but choosing text syntax, native slash parameters, and ambiguous no-target behavior affects session-state safety and command authorization semantics.

options.title: Require Explicit Target In Multi-Agent Rooms
options.body: Add text and native-command agent targeting, and make ambiguous destructive commands prompt or no-op instead of resetting a guessed agent.

options.title: Route First, Target Optional
options.body: Keep current route/binding behavior as the default and add `@agent` or native `agent:` targeting only as an override.

options.title: Document Channel Isolation Only
options.body: Leave runtime unchanged and document dedicated channels, bindings, or per-account command naming as the supported multi-agent workaround.

recommendation.title: Require Explicit Target In Multi-Agent Rooms
recommendation.body: Add text and native-command agent targeting, and make ambiguous destructive commands prompt or no-op instead of resetting a guessed agent.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest shared native-command session target history and recent command/session surface ownership signals.
